cards.text: Friend, Jonah is a prophet (2 Kings 14:25), and the last time God gave him a job, he ran to get away from the LORD (Jonah 1:3). Then a great fish vomited him onto dry land (Jonah 2:10). Now the word of the LORD comes to Jonah a second time.

cards.question: This second time, where does the LORD tell Jonah to go?

cards.text: God tells Jonah to get up, go to the great city of Nineveh, and proclaim the message He gives him. Friend, after YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, I'm the PRESIDENT of the Second Chance Club.

cards.question: This time, Jonah gets up and goes to Nineveh, just as the LORD said.

cards.text: And Nineveh is NOT a one-stoplight town, baker. The text calls it an exceedingly great city.

cards.question: A city THAT great, friend? How long a journey does Nineveh take?

cards.text: On the first day of his journey, Jonah heads into the city and starts proclaiming. And friend, the message is SHORT.

cards.question: Jonah's message says that in forty more days, Nineveh will be ___.

cards.text: Jonah proclaims, “Forty more days and Nineveh will be overturned!” EIGHT words, friend, and I've cracked open fortune cookies with longer speeches.

cards.question: Jonah says Nineveh has forty more days. How do the people of Nineveh respond?
The Ninevites proclaim a ___ and dress in ___, from the greatest of them to the least.

cards.text: From the greatest to the least, the WHOLE city is in, like a group chat where everybody actually replies. Then word reaches the king of Nineveh.

cards.question: When word reaches him, the king of Nineveh gets up from his ___ and sits in ___.

cards.text: He takes off his royal robe and goes from the throne to the ashes: not a step down, friend, the WHOLE staircase. Then he issues a proclamation in Nineveh, by the decree of the king and his nobles.

cards.question: Under the king's decree, the herds and flocks must not eat or drink either.
The king says man and beast must both be covered with sackcloth, and everyone must call out earnestly to God. What does he say each one should turn from?
The king tells the people that God will surely spare them.

cards.text: The king says, “Who knows? God may turn and relent; He may turn from His fierce anger, so that we will not perish.” Then God sees their actions, that they have turned from their evil ways.

cards.question: God sees that Nineveh has turned from its evil ways. What does He do?

answers.text: He delays it for a year

cards.text: Hang your apron up for now, friend, but don't get comfortable. This story is NOT done yet.

findings.problem: Card 7 says only that Jonah's message is short; it does not set up a warning of destruction. The baker therefore has to guess the unseen word "overturned" at the end of Jonah's line rather than reason out the blank's meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The earlier cards establish only that the Ninevites believe God. They do not introduce or imply the specific practices of proclaiming a fast and dressing in sackcloth, so both blanks test wording the baker has not seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 12 says only that word reaches the king. Although a baker might guess that a king rises from a throne, nothing in the setup establishes that he sits in ashes. The card therefore requires guessing unseen verse wording rather than reasoning out its meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
